newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures end off sharply on weak cash.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures end off sharply on weak cash.

text.p: Persistent commission house selling prompted by the weaker-than-expected tone to cash lumber knocked CME lumber futures to sharply lower closes, traders said.
Lumber closed off $6.80 per thousand board feet to unchanged with July off most at $393.80 and September off $5.00 at $383.40 per tbf.

Futures were weighed down by a weak tone to cash lumber prices, sources said. Futures had moved up recently on expectations for a spring rally in cash which had sparked technical support. But demand for lumber never developed and liquidation took futures down, traders said.
Random Lengths officially quoted cash spruce at $381 per tbf at midweek, off $1 from last Friday and $4 under last Wednesday's midweek level.
